name: ws09: auth — Tailscale provider and per-user session isolation
description:
Source
.planning/reviews/0.7.0-release-gate/09-clawft-agent-dashboard.md task #25 + Deferred Phases S3.5.
Problem / gap
The gateway only supports the local Bearer-token flow today. SPARC plan calls for a Tailscale auth provider validating X-Tailscale-User-* headers plus source-IP / cert verification, and per-user session isolation so memory / sessions / config scopes do not leak across users.
Acceptance criteria
[ ] Auth provider abstraction with Bearer (existing) and Tailscale implementations.
[ ] Tailscale provider validates X-Tailscale-User-Login, source-IP within tailnet, and (optionally) cert chain.
[ ] Per-user scoping for /api/sessions, /api/memory, /api/config so user A cannot see user B's data.
[ ] Provider selection driven by config; default remains Bearer for local-dev.
[ ] Integration tests cover an unauthorized request and a cross-user scope leak attempt.
Dependencies
use-auth hook work for the client-side scope token plumbing.
Notes
Document the threat model in a new ADR (see ADR-for-BackendAdapter task) or its own ADR.

name: ws10: voice — pocket-tts watch: adopt as fast-tier engine when official ONNX/Candle export ships
description:
Source
plan: .planning/fork-adoption-build-plan-2026-07.md §4
eval: 2026-07-07 pocket-tts evaluation (kyutai-labs/pocket-tts)
code: crates/clawft-voice-tts/src/kokoro.rs:1-18 ("No Python" invariant), crates/clawft-voice-talk/src/tts.rs:26-30 (fast-engine binding), crates/clawft-channels/src/voice/tts.rs:52-65 (TtsEngine trait)
Problem / gap
Watch item. pocket-tts (100M-param Mimi-codec streaming TTS; ~200ms TTFA and ~6x real-time on 2 CPU cores claimed; voice cloning; MIT code / gated CC-BY-4.0 weights) is a strong candidate to replace Kokoro in the fast-ack tier — and in-process synthesis would make barge-in cancel instantaneous (drop the generator) vs HTTP stream teardown, strengthening the cancel→prune→witness path. Blocked today: the official implementation is pure Python (violates the voice-tts "No Python" invariant) and community Rust/Candle/ONNX ports are unofficial single-maintainer forks. No paralinguistic tags, so it cannot take Orpheus's expressive slot.
Acceptance criteria (activation condition, then execute plan §4)
[ ] Kyutai ships an official ONNX or Candle export (or a community port gains upstream endorsement/stability)
[ ] On activation: new crates/clawft-voice-tts/src/pocket_tts.rs sibling to kokoro.rs implementing TtsEngine at TtsTier::Fast, behind onnx/candle feature
[ ] Smoke test (no weights → clean VoiceError), latency test (TTFA vs Kokoro baseline on dev hardware — adopt only if it wins), barge-in cutoff test vs current fast tier
[ ] Gated-weights provisioning (HF terms acceptance) documented in install flow
Dependencies
blocks: none
blocked-by: upstream official Rust-native export (external)
Notes
Priority low; re-check upstream quarterly or when the voice fast tier next comes under review. Full conditional build/test plan in .planning/fork-adoption-build-plan-2026-07.md §4.
